memos.headline: AAPL and XOM Lead on Relative Strength; UNH and CAT Show Deteriorating Trends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe today: AAPL and XOM are the standout leaders with strong relative strength versus SPY (+10.6%/+9.2% and +6.4%/+15.1% over 4w/12w respectively), both trading within 3% of 52-week highs with RSIs in the low 60s — healthy uptrends without overheating. On the other side, UNH is flashing warning signs with RSI at 35.5, a -7.4% gap below its 50-day mean, and -13.1% drawdown from highs despite a strong 26-week return, suggesting a trend break is underway. CAT is the weakest name in the group at -23.1% off its 52-week high with -15.3% relative underperformance over 12 weeks — this is a broken chart until it reclaims its 50-day average. MSFT's 12-week relative strength of +24% is impressive but the +9.2% extension above the 50-day mean makes me cautious on new entries here; I'd want a pullback toward the 50-day before adding.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+10.6% 4w vs SPY), only -2.3% from highs, RSI 62.8 not overbought; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~318).
Robust 12w relative strength of +15.1% vs SPY, +7.0% above 50d mean, RSI 61.6 with room to run; invalidated below ~155 (200d area).

RSI 35.5 is near oversold but the trend is clearly broken with -7.4% below 50d mean and accelerating negative relative strength; no reason to step in until RSI stabilizes above 40 and price reclaims ~408.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power dominates; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer breadth of earnings acceleration across the large-cap tech complex this quarter. NVDA posted $96.2B in quarterly revenue (+105.9% YoY) with a 62.0% net margin, GOOGL delivered a remarkable 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue (+24.2% YoY), and AMZN's net income surged 244.9% YoY to $62.65B on a 31.2% margin—all of which signal durable, expanding earnings power. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to just 4.9%, and PG saw net income decline 15.8% YoY on anemic 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% margin—both profiles I refuse to pay up for until the trajectory inflects. I would need to see XOM's next quarter show margin stabilization above 7% and PG demonstrate positive operating leverage before reconsidering.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY with 62% net margins is extraordinary earnings power; I'd reassess only if margins compress below 50%.
93.7% net margin on $119.8B revenue with nearly 4x YoY net income growth suggests a one-time gain or extraordinary operating leverage that demands ownership either way.
Net income up 245% YoY to $62.65B with margin expanding to 31.2% shows the operating leverage thesis is playing out across AWS and retail.
Full-year Q4 revenue of $90B (+17.7% YoY) with 39.7% net margin and manageable $40.3B debt reflects consistent, high-quality compounding.
Revenue +16.4% YoY to $109.4B with 27.2% net margin is solid but margin expansion lags peers; I'd want to see services mix continue rising.
Revenue +24% YoY and net income +64.9% with 17.5% margin show strong cycle momentum, though I'd watch backlog data for sustainability.
Revenue +27.7% and NI +41.2% are impressive but $460.5B total debt and cyclical credit risk keep me neutral until I see provision trends.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) with only 4.9% net margin despite NI rebounding 61%—I need to see top-line re-acceleration before getting constructive.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin is classic cash-flow compression; I'd reconsider if margins recover above 7%.
Revenue +1.5% and net income -15.8% with margin slipping to 14.4% signals negative operating leverage in a staples name I won't pay a premium for.

memos.headline: Fed Paused but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Surging 10y Yields Create a Hostile Backdrop for Duration and Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months after cutting 75bp over the prior year, yet headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY—well above target—while the 10y yield has spiked 95bp over 12 months to 4.96%, flattening the 10y-2y spread to just 39bp. The labor market remains firm with unemployment at 4.1%, down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons, which removes any urgency for the Fed to ease further and may even reopen a tightening discussion if inflation stays sticky. This combination of elevated long rates and persistent inflation is a headwind for long-duration growth equities and rate-sensitive cyclicals, while banks can benefit from a positively sloped curve and stable short rates, and defensive staples should hold up. A CPI print falling toward 2.5% or an unemployment spike above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Positive curve slope, stable fed funds, and strong labor market support net interest margins and credit quality.
Defensive staple with pricing power should outperform in a sticky-inflation, high-rate pause environment.
Firm economy and inflation hedge appeal are offset by risk that high rates slow global demand; no strong directional call.
Long-duration growth equity faces valuation compression as the 10y yield approaches 5% with no near-term easing catalyst.
Same duration headwind as AAPL; 95bp rise in 10y yields over 12 months pressures high-multiple tech.
Highest-beta duration name in the universe; 4.96% 10y yield is a significant discount-rate headwind.
Consumer spending resilience from low unemployment partially offsets the long-duration valuation drag.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP growth may hold up, but elevated rates cap multiple expansion.
Cyclical capex name vulnerable if high rates begin to bite investment spending; curve flattening is a warning.
Defensive healthcare but regulatory uncertainty and modest rate sensitivity leave me without strong conviction.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT/AMZN/NVDA Momentum vs. AAPL/GOOGL Drag Persists Into September
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in sentiment across mega-cap tech coming out of Q2/Q3 earnings season. MSFT (+15.5%), AMZN (+15.3%), and NVDA (+8.7%) all posted strongly positive price reactions to their results, suggesting the market narrative around AI monetization and cloud strength remains firmly intact for these names. Conversely, AAPL (-7.4%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) saw sharp post-earnings selloffs that have not been accompanied by any obvious positive narrative reset since—AAPL's subsequent 8-K/A on director changes and GOOGL's August 'Other Events' filing are unlikely catalysts to reverse negative tone. On the industrial side, CAT's +5.6% earnings reaction and a new material agreement in September suggest constructive sentiment, while PG's mild -1.9% decline and flurry of Reg FD filings point to a defensive name treading water. I have lower conviction on JPM and UNH given the absence of earnings-reaction data in the evidence and only procedural filings to work with.

views.note: Massive +15.5% post-earnings pop signals a strong positive narrative shift; September Reg FD filing suggests continued proactive investor engagement.
+15.3% earnings reaction is the strongest positive sentiment signal in the universe; recent director change filing is routine and unlikely to disrupt momentum.
+8.7% earnings pop plus new material agreement and follow-on 'Other Events' filing suggest sustained positive narrative around AI capex cycle.
-7.4% earnings selloff with no subsequent positive catalyst; director change 8-K/A is unlikely to shift negative tone.
-7.1% post-earnings drop and only a generic 'Other Events' filing since; no evidence of narrative recovery.
+5.6% earnings reaction and a new material definitive agreement suggest constructive industrial sentiment, though conviction is moderate given sector cyclicality.
Mild -1.9% earnings reaction and multiple Reg FD filings suggest a defensive name with no clear directional sentiment catalyst.
Only procedural bylaw and 'Other Events' filings with no earnings reaction data; insufficient signal to take a directional view.
Single Reg FD filing with no earnings reaction data available; sentiment is opaque and I have no edge here.
No filings or sentiment data in the evidence set; cannot form a view.

memos.headline: Surging Policy Uncertainty and $103 Oil Signal Geopolitical Stress; NVDA and XOM Most Exposed
memos.body: I am flagging a sharp deterioration in the geopolitical-policy backdrop: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has spiked to 466.83, up 63% in one month and 151% over three months, a level historically associated with major sanctions episodes or trade-war escalations. WTI crude at $103.57 (+24% m/m) reinforces that energy-security risks—whether from Middle East disruption, Russia-related sanctions enforcement, or OPEC+ supply management—are intensifying. Notably, credit spreads (HY OAS at 2.70%) remain benign and VIX at 17.84 is elevated only modestly, suggesting markets have not fully priced the policy tail risk embedded in the uncertainty index. NVDA filed two 8-Ks in rapid succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3), which in the current environment I read as likely related to export-control or China-policy disclosures; I lack the text but the cadence is unusual and warrants caution. My conviction is highest on XOM benefiting from the energy-security premium and lowest on NVDA given semiconductor export-control overhang; I would need a concrete de-escalation in US-China chip restrictions or a sustained drop in the EPU index below 300 to change my view.

views.note: $103 WTI and rising energy-security concerns provide a structural tailwind; oil up 24% in a month signals geopolitical supply risk, not just demand.
Two 8-K filings in three weeks amid a 151% surge in policy uncertainty suggest possible export-control or China-related disclosures that could constrain revenue.
Heavy China supply-chain concentration is a structural vulnerability at this EPU level, but no company-specific filing to confirm near-term action; staying neutral until clarity emerges.
Infrastructure and energy capex cycles tend to benefit from geopolitical supply-security spending; Aug 4 Reg FD filing may relate to order-book strength.
Sanctions enforcement and trade-finance complexity can boost fee income but also compliance costs; benign credit spreads keep me neutral for now.
Sep 2 Reg FD filing amid elevated policy uncertainty could relate to government-cloud or AI-export matters; insufficient detail to take a directional view.
